basis: Mandibulofacial dysostosis and hearing loss 5/6; cleft palate 3/6 and airway failure 3/6. Eyelid coloboma 3/6 omitted at cap in favor of feeding/airway damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate in 3/6 causes structural oral dysfunction; feeding difficulties occur in 5/6.
decisions.ocular: none: eyelid coloboma occurs in 3/6, but feeding and ventilatory impairment take priority under the four-axis cap.

basis: Defining neurodevelopmental, cataract and skin/hair disease; ASD 2/6 (~33%). Mild toe syndactyly 3/5 and cleft palate 2/6 omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: atrial septal defect in 2/6 (~33%) is direct structural cardiac disease; retained for potential functional severity.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: toe syndactyly occurs in 3/5 but is a minor skeletal defect; more consequential cardiac disease takes the final slot.

basis: Storage disease with core cytopenias and cardiac defects/failure (11/13); nephrosis 4/5, proteinuria 20/20. Skeletal, CNS, pulmonary and hepatic findings omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital cardiac defects are a defining component; heart failure 11/13 and cardiomyopathy 9/13 make cardiac disease a severe core manifestation.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: dysostosis and contractures occur in 20/20 and 18/18, but severe cardiac, renal and haematologic disease take priority under the cap.

basis: Congenital peripheral hypomyelination; typical distal muscle atrophy and fixed foot deformity (>30%) cause lasting structural loss. Respiratory weakness alone is not lung damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent distal muscle atrophy and structural foot deformities are typical in most patients, constituting tissue loss/deformity within CMT rather than weakness alone.

basis: Interferon-mediated encephalopathy; chilblains ~40%, eyelid coloboma HPO 30-79%. Frequent transaminitis/hepatomegaly do not establish lasting liver damage; glaucoma <30%.

decisions.hepatic: none: frequent hepatomegaly/transaminitis can be transient; the record does not establish lasting hepatic damage in at least 30%.
decisions.ocular: involved: eyelid coloboma is a structural eyelid defect, explicitly annotated frequent (30-79%); glaucoma alone is below 30%.

basis: Diabetes, optic atrophy and deafness are cardinal; hearing loss 60-90%. Hydronephrosis 8/10 (80%); neurologic dysfunction ~33-50% omitted at cap.

decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural deafness is a cardinal component of Wolfram/DIDMOAD, with hearing impairment in 60-90% in the supplied series.

basis: Neurodevelopmental/myelination disorder; hearing loss 43-50%, skeletal abnormalities and GH deficiency 30-79%. Cardiac and ocular findings omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac defects are annotated 30-79%, but the cap favors characteristic hearing, skeletal and endocrine dysfunction across the syndrome.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: secondary growth hormone deficiency is annotated frequent (30-79%) and represents endocrine loss of function, beyond short stature alone.

basis: Core skeletal, nail and renal dysplasia (CKD 2/2); retinal dystrophy with progressive visual loss 1/1 assessed. Dental defects 2/2 omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: primary: inherited renal tubular disease is part of the defining ancestry; tubulointerstitial nephritis and stage 3 CKD occur in 2/2 assessed patients.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder with epilepsy; strabismus 8/14 (~57%). Constipation and dental spacing/retention do not establish destructive or disabling GI disease.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: constipation 14/22 and dental spacing/retention do not establish direct GI tissue injury or substantial loss of oral function; feeding difficulty alone is insufficient.

basis: Osteosclerosis and brain abnormalities define disease; lung hypoplasia 4/7 (~57%), cleft palate 80-99%, gingival fibromatosis 30-79%. Hearing/urinary defects <30%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate (80-99%) and gingival fibromatosis (30-79%) are common structural oral disease, accompanying the defining bone and brain disorder.
